elements.name: NullPacker
elements.description: A no-op packer for headless tests and the pre-renderer bring-up: it accepts every placement and reports an empty ripple. Lets the command-model core run without the layout engine present.

elements.name: RepackResult
elements.description: What a re-pack disturbed, so the renderer can bound the animation per feasibility A1. Layout cost itself is off the frame loop; only this animation touches the frame.

elements.name: SetAbstractCommand
elements.description: Toggle the abstract modifier (§3.1). Glyph switches to outline/wireframe in the renderer.

elements.name: IPacker
elements.description: The packer owns position, not the user (ADR-003; authoring-ux.md §0.1). The authoring layer never sets an xyz — it tells the packer "this element is now a child of that parent" and the packer assigns the position and gently re-packs the affected subtree (siblings preserved, no pop). This is the single most important authoring invariant: there is no free-position gesture because there is no free space. Implemented by the layout engine (rendering-and-vr.md §2.1, off the frame loop). The returned RepackResult lets the renderer drive the comfort-bounded cross-fade (feasibility A1: animate the affected subtree only, ease ≤300ms, alpha-fade nodes that move > ~10°).

elements.name: IBubblePicker
elements.description: Resolves a pick ray to a model element. Implemented by the render/layout side over the BVH (rendering-and-vr.md §3.5: "BVH is the picking companion for VR controller rays", O(log n)). The authoring layer depends only on this seam, never on the renderer — so the command-model core (modes, validity, undo) is testable with a fake picker and the real BVH drops in unchanged. Feasibility note (ticket 31036022, §7 C1): the riskiest VR interaction is picking a small, deep child bubble. Mitigations live behind this seam: the implementer applies an angular magnetic assist (snap to the nearest valid endpoint within an angular radius) and one-euro ray smoothing, and flags assisted picks via Assisted so the UI can show the dwell-to-confirm candidate highlight before commit. The  predicate lets the picker bias the assist toward legal targets so it never snaps to an illegal one.

elements.name: EndAnchor
elements.description: A fixed endpoint attachment: a side of the box and a 0..1 position along that side.

elements.name: ContainmentRules
elements.description: Containment legality (authoring-ux.md §3.1 "containment-filtered"). Answers "may a child of kind live directly inside parentKind?" — the rule the creation palette dims an illegal chip on, and that add-node enforces. UML class/bubble core only for v1.

elements.name: PickResult
elements.description: The element a ray resolved to, plus the surface point and whether an assist was applied.

elements.name: EdgeRules
elements.description: Edge legality, kind-aware and "felt during the drag" (authoring-ux.md §4.4). Edges in v1 connect classifiers (and packages, for dependency), never members. Self-edges, generalization typing, and generalization cycles are checked here so the §B invalid affordance fires before the drop.

elements.name: SourceFileDto
elements.description: One imported source file's original text, keyed by its path — backs the overlay round-trip.

elements.name: UmlCanvas4
elements.description: Save / load of the whole diagram — model (classifiers, members, edges with language/stereotype and multiplicities) plus all geometry/view-state (positions, sizes, orthogonal routes, endpoint pins). Written as JSON to DiagramPath. Load rebuilds through the public command API and remaps the saved ids to freshly-minted ones (the model assembly's internals aren't reachable from the view).

elements.name: UmlCanvas5
elements.description: The interactive standard-UML editor harness. A tab bar selects the active package; the canvas shows that package's classifiers as UML boxes with member compartments (fields/methods inside). Right-click / ctrl-click adds containment-filtered elements (§3.1) with a name prompt (§3.5); dragging a node's connect handle draws a relationship with a valid-kind type picker and proper UML arrowheads (§4.2/§4.4); boxes drag to move and resize from the corner grip; Ctrl/Cmd+Z / +Shift+Z undo/redo (§1). Desktop stand-in for the DOTS bubble renderer — the harness owns 2D layout, the real packer owns 3D (ADR-003). The authoring core (model/rules/commands/controller) is reused unchanged.

elements.name: AuthoringController
elements.description: The input-agnostic authoring state machine — the shared brain behind both the desktop toolbar and the VR radial (authoring-ux.md §1–§4 at full parity). Desktop (Input System) and VR (XRI) adapters call the same verbs here; this class owns mode, spring-loaded commit style, target validity, and routes every mutation through the UndoStack. It holds no engine/render references — only the IPacker and IBubblePicker seams — so it unit-tests as plain C#. Invariants enforced here: • Never stranded (§1): Cancel always returns to Select. • Placement = pick the parent (§0.1): add/connect only ever resolve an element, never a coordinate. • Validity felt before commit (§3.1/§4.4): commits are refused on an invalid target. • Spring-loaded (§1): one-shot auto-returns to Select; sticky stays until cancel.

elements.name: Float3
elements.description: A minimal 3-vector. The authoring assembly is engine-free (so the command/rules core unit-tests as plain C#); the renderer adapter converts between this and UnityEngine.Vector3 at the seam.

elements.name: Ray3
elements.description: A pick ray: origin + (assumed-normalized) direction. Desktop = camera ray; VR = controller ray.

elements.name: AffordanceState
elements.description: The reserved UI-state channel (authoring-ux.md §5.1 "the critical call"). Authoring feedback must NOT reuse kind hues — a green "valid" glow would read as function. This enum is the state; the renderer maps it to the reserved achromatic + vermillion channel and the shape cue (every state is encoded ≥2× per §5.2, never color alone). Identical in desktop and VR (§6).

elements.name: KindInfo
elements.description: Static metadata about kinds. The hue strings are the §2.1 Okabe-Ito palette tokens; the renderer maps them to materials. Kept here (not in the renderer) so the authoring palette and the bubble show the same kind the same way without a translation step (§3.1, §5).

elements.name: UmlEdge3D
elements.description: A relationship drawn in 3-D as a world-space polyline (a LineRenderer) following a route the integration layer computes. The 3-D counterpart of UmlEdgeView's segment chain: SetRoute feeds it the world points and a color; SetArrow toggles a small cone arrowhead at the last point, oriented along the final segment. Dashed relationship kinds (dependency, realization, «include»/«extend», note anchors, reply messages) draw with true dashes via a tiled 1-px dash texture on the line material; the tiling is scaled to the route's total world length so dash density is uniform regardless of length.

elements.name: CommitStyle
elements.description: Spring-loaded behaviour (§1): tap = place/draw one then auto-return to Select; hold/lock = sticky until cancel. Default is OneShot — a mode that silently eats your next click is the most common way diagram tools confuse people.

elements.name: AuthoringMode
elements.description: The command surface's home-and-modes (authoring-ux.md §1). Select is home and is never owned by the authoring surface as a "mode" you can be trapped in; Add/Connect are the only spring-loaded modes. delete/undo/redo/project are instantaneous and do not appear here (they never become a mode).

elements.name: Validity
elements.description: The result of a legality check. Carries a human reason so the UI can show the §B invalid affordance (vermillion dashed rim + ✕) with a hover reason "at point-of-use rather than as a failed drop" (authoring-ux.md §3.1). A rule that is satisfied returns Valid; the reason is empty.

elements.name: UmlBackground
elements.description: Full-canvas backdrop: empty-space clicks (add menu / deselect). A plain drag rubber-band-selects nodes; a Ctrl/Cmd-drag pans the diagram instead. The mode is latched at drag-start so a modifier released mid-drag doesn't switch gestures.

elements.name: UmlLayerMarker
elements.description: The "this relationship continues on another z-layer" glyph: a small chevron (▲ above / ▼ below) seated at the far end of a cross-layer stub, where the off-layer endpoint has been culled (UmlCanvas Z-layer view). Drawn as a procedural triangle Image tinted the link color so it reads as part of the line. Clicking it jumps the canvas to the layer the hidden endpoint lives on, so the user can "follow" the connector.

elements.name: IIdFactory
elements.description: Mints stable ids for new elements/edges. Default uses GUIDs; the real pipeline uses qualified-name hashes.

elements.name: SetDescriptionCommand
elements.description: Set an element's free-text description / documentation (fed to code generation). One reversible undo step; captures the prior value.

elements.name: CountingIdFactory
elements.description: Deterministic-enough default id source. Monotonic counter avoids collisions without a clock.

elements.name: AuthoringCoreTests
elements.description: EditMode tests for the engine-agnostic authoring core (authoring-ux.md §0–§4). These validate the invariants the whole authoring surface depends on: containment + edge legality, single-step undo, spring-loaded modes, and never-stranded cancel. No renderer / XR required — the core is pure C#.

elements.name: ICallbacks
elements.description: Callbacks in the TestRunnerApi for the test stages when running tests.

elements.name: ReParentCommand
elements.description: Re-parent — the only "move" gesture (§3.6). Packer re-packs both old and new parent.

elements.name: UmlNoteGraphic
elements.description: A UML note background: a rectangle whose top-right corner is actually clipped off (a pentagon), with the folded-over flap drawn in a darker shade. Outline effects then trace the clipped silhouette.

elements.name: NodeStyle
elements.description: An optional per-element visual override (fill / border / text color, font, size). Has=false → defaults.

elements.name: TestRunnerApi
elements.description: The TestRunnerApi retrieves and runs tests programmatically from code inside the project, or inside other packages. TestRunnerApi is a [ScriptableObject](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/ScriptableObject.html). You can initialize the API like this: var testRunnerApi = ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<TestRunnerApi>(); Note: You can subscribe and receive test results in one instance of the API, even if the run starts from another instance. The TestRunnerApi supports the following workflows: - [How to run tests programmatically](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.1/manual/extension-run-tests.html) - [How to get test results](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.1/manual/extension-get-test-results.html) - [How to retrieve the list of tests](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.1/manual/extension-retrieve-test-list.html)

elements.name: UmlConnectHandle
elements.description: A per-side connect hotspot: drag from it to start a relationship that leaves from that side.

elements.name: ModelElement
elements.description: One element (node) in the unified model: a kind, a name, a containment parent, and modifiers.

elements.name: UmlResizeHandle
elements.description: The bottom-right resize grip: dragging it resizes the node (vs. the body, which moves).

elements.name: UndoStack
elements.description: The authoring history. Executing a command runs it and pushes it onto the undo stack, clearing the redo stack (standard linear history). Undo/Redo are the instantaneous §1 verbs — never modes. Toolbar Undo/Redo dim from CanUndo/CanRedo (authoring-ux.md §2.2).

elements.name: ElementKind
elements.description: The UML class/bubble-core element kinds for v1 (authoring-ux.md §3.1). These are the kinds the code→model reverse-engineering pipeline produces; the patterns generalize to other notations later. Order matches the creation-palette table; Class is the palette default.

elements.name: UmlCameraRig
elements.description: A full 6-DOF camera rig for the 3-D diagram. It owns a perspective Camera and recomputes its transform every LateUpdate from a small piece of state — Yaw, Pitch, Roll, Distance — around a focus Pivot. The camera sits on the +Z side of the pivot looking back toward −Z, so by convention it views the nodes' front (+Z) faces (where the text/content lives) at the default pose. The integration layer drives it imperatively through Uml3DScene: orbit on drag, dolly on scroll, pan with a modifier, roll with Q/E, free-fly translate with WASD/RF, and Frame to fit the whole diagram in view. Add it to a GameObject (it creates its own child camera in Awake if one isn't supplied) and it is immediately usable.

elements.name: DeleteEdgeCommand
elements.description: Delete a relationship edge as a single undo step (§4.6).

elements.name: TestMode
elements.description: A flag indicating whether to run Edit Mode or Play Mode tests.

elements.name: ITestAdaptor
elements.description: ```ITestAdaptor``` is a representation of a node in the test tree implemented as a wrapper around the [NUnit](http://www.nunit.org/) [ITest](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/master/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Interfaces/ITest.cs)  interface.

elements.name: CommandContext
elements.description: What a command operates on: the model, the packer (position/re-pack), and the id source.

elements.name: Filter
elements.description: The filter class provides the TestRunnerApi with a specification of what tests to run when [running tests programmatically](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@1.1/manual/extension-run-tests.html).

elements.name: IAuthoringCommand
elements.description: One reversible authoring mutation. Every authoring verb is exactly one of these so it is a single undo step (authoring-ux.md §0.2). Do must capture whatever Undo needs to restore the prior state precisely.

elements.name: AddNodeCommand
elements.description: Add a node as a child of parent (placement = pick the parent, §0.1/§3). Packer positions it.

elements.name: SetSourceFileCommand
elements.description: Set an element's originating source file path (folder import / overlay round-trip). One reversible undo step; captures the prior value.

elements.name: DeleteElementCommand
elements.description: Delete an element and its whole subtree plus every incident edge, as a single undo step (§4.6/§3.6). Snapshots everything removed so Undo restores the subtree and edges exactly.

elements.name: SetMetaCommand
elements.description: Set classifier metadata — implementation language and a custom stereotype override (Rational Rose / Sparx EA classifier properties). One reversible undo step; captures the prior values.

elements.name: SetZLayerCommand
elements.description: Set an element's diagram z-layer (0 = base). One reversible undo step; captures the prior value.

elements.name: MemberParts
elements.description: The structured form of a member signature, decomposed from / composed to the canonical Rose/Sparx text convention the model stores verbatim in Name — e.g. - balance : decimal or + deposit(amount : decimal) : void {abstract}. The view's structured editor builds and reads this so the user picks visibility/type/params from controls instead of hand-typing UML punctuation.

elements.name: ConnectCommand
elements.description: Connect two elements with a relationship (§4). Direction is from→to.

elements.name: RunState
elements.description: The RunState enum indicates whether a test can be executed.

elements.name: Uml3DConfig
elements.description: Shared constants and the model→world coordinate contract for the 3-D diagram scene. The flat uGUI renderer (UmlCanvas) lays nodes out in UI pixels; the 3-D scene multiplies those by WorldScale so a conventional 220-px class box becomes ≈2.2 world units wide. Z-layering (the bubble-view "below / behind" stacking) is expressed as an integer layerDepth — the signed distance from the active layer — multiplied by LayerGap. Keeping all of this in one place means the camera rig, node, edge and scene code agree on units without a translation step.

elements.name: TargetEvaluation
elements.description: How a candidate target reads right now: the §5.1 affordance, the resolved parent/endpoint, and a reason.

elements.name: IErrorCallbacks
elements.description: An extended version of the ICallbacks, which get invoked if the test run fails due to a build error or if any IPrebuildSetup has a failure.

elements.name: UmlShapeGraphic
elements.description: Draws use-case (ellipse), state (rounded rect), start/final markers (disc / ring), and actors (stick figure).

elements.name: SetCodeCommand
elements.description: Set an element's saved source code (the approved "Generate code" output). Undoable.

elements.name: RenameCommand
elements.description: Rename an element (§3.5). Empty name is a caller concern (deduped default); this just sets it.

elements.name: Uml3DScene
elements.description: The manager the integration layer drives to render a UML diagram as a real 3-D scene. It does not read the authoring model directly (UmlCanvas owns that); instead it exposes an imperative API: add / remove nodes and edges, raycast the scene to pick a node, and pass orbit / dolly / pan / frame commands through to its UmlCameraRig. On Awake it builds the rig (on a child), a DiagramRoot transform that all nodes/edges parent under, and a directional light so the lit node material is visible.

elements.name: UmlModalBackdrop
elements.description: Dim modal backdrop behind a property/member dialog: a click on the dim area cancels the dialog. The dim backdrop behind a modal property dialog. It exists only to BLOCK pointer events from reaching the canvas/nodes underneath — it intentionally does NOT dismiss the dialog on click. Property dialogs close only via their explicit OK / Cancel buttons (a stray click outside must not discard in-progress edits).

elements.name: HandleRole
elements.description: What a handle drives.

elements.name: SetEdgeMetaCommand
elements.description: Set a relationship's adornments — midpoint label (association name / role) and the per-end source/target multiplicities (e.g. "1", "0..*"). One reversible undo step.

elements.name: UmlNode3D
elements.description: A real 3-D UML node: a procedurally-built box slab (a 12-triangle cuboid) whose front (+Z) face carries a world-space uGUI canvas reproducing the classifier compartments — stereotype, bold name, an attributes block, a divider, then an operations block — a faithful-enough port of UmlNodeView's layout. The slab is lit (URP/Lit, with Standard and unlit fallbacks) and tinted with the node fill color; a BoxCollider matching the slab makes it pickable via Physics raycasts. The integration layer drives it imperatively: Init to build, SetWorldPose to place it on its layer, AddLocalRotation to spin the individual node, SetSelected for the selection highlight, and SetDepthTint to gray out below-layer nodes. A collider hit maps back to this component via GetComponentInParent<UmlNode3D>.

elements.name: ReTypeEdgeCommand
elements.description: Change a relationship's type in place (§4.6 re-type).

elements.name: UmlVisibility
elements.description: UML member visibility (Rational Rose / Sparx EA "scope"): the leading glyph on an attribute or operation.

elements.name: EndMarker
elements.description: End decoration for a relationship line, in standard UML notation.

elements.name: EdgeKind
elements.description: The UML relationship edge kinds. The first six are class-diagram relationships; the rest carry the behavioral / cross-diagram connectors (state & activity flow, use-case include/extend, note anchors, directed associations) so every node type gets a relationship that shows the correct direction (§4.2). Appended so saved-diagram edge ordinals stay stable.

elements.name: UmlEdgeView
elements.description: A standard-UML relationship drawn as an orthogonal (right-angle) polyline between two class boxes: solid or dashed, with the correct end markers (open arrow, hollow inheritance triangle, hollow/filled aggregation-composition diamond), a midpoint association label, and per-end multiplicities. The route is a list of points the canvas computes (auto-routed or via user bend handles); this view just draws one segment rect per leg and seats the markers/labels along the first and last legs. Left-click selects (the canvas shows bend handles); right-click / ctrl-click re-types, adorns, or deletes (§4.6).

elements.name: UmlHandleKind
elements.description: What an edge handle controls: a pinned endpoint, a movable bend, or an "insert bend here" spot.

elements.name: UmlEdgeHandle
elements.description: A handle on the selected relationship. Endpoint handles re-pin where the line meets a box (drag anywhere on its border); Vertex handles move a bend (drag) or delete it (right-click); Add handles insert a new bend at a segment midpoint (click). The canvas owns the geometry; this relays the gesture.

elements.name: UmlImageClipboard
elements.description: Writes a diagram snapshot to disk and pushes it onto the OS clipboard as an image. On macOS the PNG is placed on the pasteboard via osascript (so it pastes straight into Keynote / Slack / docs); on other platforms the file path is copied instead (the system copy buffer is text-only there).

elements.name: ITestRunSettings
elements.description: ITestRunSettings lets you set any of the global settings right before building a Player for a test run and then reverts the settings afterward. ITestRunSettings implements [IDisposable](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.idisposable?view=netframework-4.8), and runs after building the Player with tests.

elements.name: RetargetEdgeCommand
elements.description: Re-home one endpoint of an edge (§4.6 re-target). Keeps the edge's type.

elements.name: UmlEdgeHandle3D
elements.description: A small draggable 3-D sphere used to edit the route of the selected link. The 3-D counterpart of the flat renderer's UmlEdgeHandle: the integration layer (UmlCanvas) spawns one per editable point on the selected edge — interior waypoints and segment midpoints (the polyline editing affordances) plus the two endpoint anchors (where the link meets each node face). A scene Physics raycast that hits the sphere maps back to this component via GetComponentInParent<UmlEdgeHandle3D>; the canvas then reads Edge, Index and Role to know what the drag should move.

elements.name: BoxSide
elements.description: The four box sides a relationship can attach to / leave from.

elements.name: UmlColorWheelGraphic
elements.description: A procedural HSV hue/saturation disc, drawn at full value (V=1): hue runs around the rim, saturation runs from white at the centre to fully-saturated at the rim. The mesh is a triangle fan so it stays crisp at any size without a texture. Click or drag anywhere on the disc to pick a hue/saturation pair — the chosen value is reported through OnHueSat as (hue, saturation) both normalised to 0..1. Brightness (value) and alpha are not part of the disc; the style picker composes them with separate sliders.

elements.name: UmlMemberSignature
elements.description: Compose / parse the canonical UML member signature string used by Rational Rose, Sparx EA, and most UML tools. Pure C# (no Unity dependency) so it unit-tests directly and round-trips through the editor.

elements.name: EdgeId
elements.description: Stable identity for an edge (relationship). Edges are model objects, not drawn artifacts (§0.2).

elements.name: UmlNodeView
elements.description: A standard-UML classifier box (class / interface / enum / struct) with three compartments — stereotype+name, attributes (fields), operations (methods) — so members render inside the box, not as separate nodes. Ctrl/Cmd-drag the body to move it (a plain drag is reserved for the background marquee), the right-edge handle drags to draw a relationship (§4.1), and the bottom-right grip drags to resize. Left-click selects; Shift+left-click toggles the multi-selection; right-click opens the add-member / delete menu (§3.1).

elements.name: ElementId
elements.description: Stable identity for a model element. The value is the element's stable key (qualified-name hash, rendering-and-vr.md §2.1 "stable addresses") so a node keeps its identity — and roughly its packed position — across edits and re-derivation. Authoring commands address elements by this id, never by transient array index or scene-object reference.

elements.name: ModelEdge
elements.description: One relationship (edge) in the unified model. Direction is from→to (§4.2).

elements.name: AuthoringModel
elements.description: The in-memory unified model that authoring verbs mutate (authoring-ux.md §0.2: every verb is a model edit; all views are re-derived from this). This type owns the containment tree and the edge list and enforces structural integrity (a node has exactly one parent; ids are unique). It does not own geometry — positions/radii are the packer's job (ADR-003) and live behind IPacker. Mutators are deliberately low-level and reversible so the command layer (§0.2 "each is a single undo step") can compose and unwind them precisely.

elements.name: TestStatus
elements.description: The TestStatus enum indicates the test result status.

elements.name: UmlPaletteItem
elements.description: A toolbar palette entry: click to add at center, or drag onto the canvas to drop a new node.

elements.name: ITestResultAdaptor
elements.description: The `ITestResultAdaptor` is the representation of the test results for a node in the test tree implemented as a wrapper around the [NUnit](http://www.nunit.org/) [ITest](https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/master/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Interfaces/ITestResults.cs) interface.

elements.name: UmlShape
elements.description: The procedural shapes used by non-class UML nodes.

elements.name: ExecutionSettings
elements.description: A set of execution settings defining how to run tests, using the TestRunnerApi.

elements.name: AllocatingGCMemoryConstraint
elements.description: An NUnit test constraint class to test whether a given block of code makes any GC allocations. Use this class with NUnit's Assert.That() method to make assertions about the GC behaviour of your code. The constraint executes the delegate you provide, and checks if it has caused any GC memory to be allocated. If any GC memory was allocated, the constraint passes; otherwise, the constraint fails. Usually you negate this constraint to make sure that your delegate does not allocate any GC memory. This is easy to do using the Is class: using NUnit.Framework; using UnityEngine.TestTools.Constraints; using Is = UnityEngine.TestTools.Constraints.Is; public class MyTestClass { [Test] public void SettingAVariableDoesNotAllocate() { Assert.That(() => { int a = 0; a = 1; }, Is.Not.AllocatingGCMemory()); } }

elements.name: CodeGenContext
elements.description: Everything the code generator needs about one element: its identity (name / kind / language / stereotype / abstract), its members (attribute + operation signature strings as the model stores them), the text of any UML notes attached to it, and its relationships to other elements (collaborators it uses, callers, and the base classes / interfaces it extends or implements). Plain data — the UmlCanvas partial walks the model to populate it. ToPromptString renders it as a structured block for the LLM, and the deterministic CodeSkeleton consumes the same fields for the offline fallback.

elements.name: RelKind
elements.description: How an element relates to a collaborator (a supertype, an interface, a used type, or a caller).

elements.name: LlmClient
elements.description: A tiny, dependency-free client for an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint. Builds the request with JsonUtility (no System.Text.Json in the player runtime) and parses the first choice's message content back out. The caller owns the UnityWebRequest lifecycle (send it inside a coroutine and dispose it); this class only constructs and parses.

elements.name: ConstraintExtensions
elements.description: An NUnit test constraint class to test whether a given block of code makes any GC allocations.

elements.name: RequirePlatformSupportAttribute
elements.description: The `RequirePlatformSupportAttribute` attribute can be applied to test assemblies (will affect every test in the assembly), fixtures (will affect every test in the fixture), or to individual test methods.

elements.name: UmlCanvas
elements.description: The "Generate code" feature: turns a UML element into source. A deterministic offline skeleton (CodeSkeleton) is shown immediately, then — if an LLM endpoint is configured (LlmSettings) — an OpenAI-compatible chat request refines it in place. The generation context (CodeGenContext) folds in the element's members, its Description, the text of any UML notes attached to it, and its relationships (collaborators it uses / is used by, plus the base classes and interfaces it extends / implements, each carrying the collaborator's member API). Reuses the canvas's model (_model) and modal/menu helpers from the other partials.

elements.name: AuthoringDemoBootstrap
elements.description: Runtime entry point for the on-screen authoring harness. Stands up a camera + EventSystem and a single UmlCanvas that builds the interactive 2D UML editor and drives the real AuthoringController (Assets/Scripts/Authoring). It is a desktop stand-in for the (gated) DOTS bubble renderer — same command model, 2D boxes instead of 3D bubbles — so the authoring core is visible and usable today. The production surface is the UI Toolkit toolbar + VR radial (authoring-ux.md §2).

elements.name: LogAssert
elements.description: `LogAssert` lets you expect Unity log messages that would otherwise cause the test to fail. A test fails if Unity logs a message other than a regular log or warning message. Use `LogAssert` to check for an expected message in the log so that the test does not fail when Unity logs the message. Use `LogAssert.Expect` before running the code under test, as the check for expected logs runs at the end of each frame. A test also reports a failure, if an expected message does not appear, or if Unity does not log any regular log or warning messages.

elements.name: ParsedModel
elements.description: The root object — a named array so JsonUtility can deserialize it.

elements.name: Is
elements.description: NUnit allows you to write test assertions in a more descriptive and human readable way using the Assert.That mechanism, where the first parameter is an object under test and the second parameter describes conditions that the object has to meet. We have extended NUnit API with a custom constraint type and declared an overlay Is class. To resolve ambiguity between the original implementation and the custom one you must explicitly declare it with a using statement or via addressing through the full type name `UnityEngine.TestTools.Constraints.Is`.

elements.name: ComingSoonBootstrap
elements.description: Temporary placeholder splash for The Robot Draft. Builds a dark overlay with a "Coming Soon" title and an Exit button at runtime, and forces the standalone player into a resizable window. It is intentionally dependency-free: no scene wiring, no asset references, no render-pipeline setup — it runs automatically on Play and in a built player via RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod, so the project renders correctly on the very first try. This is a stub. The production shell will be a URP + Render Graph project with a UI Toolkit front-end and the DOTS/OpenXR bubble-view renderer described in docs/specs/unity-6.3-baseline.md and ADR-001. Replace this class when that shell lands.

elements.name: LlmSettings

elements.description: Mei #2 (seq493): resolved options for `dynamic` facets, keyed by filter key. DataTable doesn't fetch domain options itself (it can't know how); the page resolves them (e.g. api.listProjects) and injects them here.

elements.name: + embedded : boolean
elements.description: Embedded related mini-table: drops the filter/pagination chrome, fixed scope.

elements.name: + scope : Record<string, unknown>
elements.description: Extra api.list opts (related-table scope query, or a parent facet).

elements.name: + onOpenRow : (row: T)
elements.description: Row opened (primary-cell click or Enter) → detail.

elements.name: + onEdit : (row: T)
elements.description: Open the edit form for this row (omit when not editable).

elements.name: + options : FacetOption[]
elements.description: Static facet options. Omit when the options are resolved dynamically (see `dynamic`).

elements.name: + dynamic : boolean
elements.description: Marks a facet whose options the primitive must resolve at runtime (e.g. projects).

elements.name: + multi : boolean
elements.description: Multi-select facet: the user picks several values (OR-within-facet); the selected values pass to api.list as an ARRAY under `key`. Default false (single ). BE must accept the array param for the key.

elements.name: + span : boolean
elements.description: Full-width (long/rich fields: description, body).

elements.name: + render : CellRenderer<T>
elements.description: Cell render: a registry hint string or a function.

elements.name: + initial : Record<string, unknown>
elements.description: Edit mode: the current row's values. Create: omit (fields start empty).

elements.name: + referenceOptions : Record<string, FacetOption[]>
elements.description: Resolved options for `dynamic` select/reference fields, keyed by field key.

elements.name: + onSubmit : (values: Record<string, unknown>)
elements.description: The page wires this to descriptor.api.create/update + a refresh. May throw to trigger keep-input-on-failure.

elements.name: + onBack : ()
elements.description: Back-with-state: the page owns history/scroll restoration.

elements.name: + orgId : string
elements.description: Identifier the `api.*` methods expect (the org UUID — api is UUID-keyed).

elements.name: + orgSlug : string
elements.description: Canonical org SLUG for building app routes (/app//…). Distinct from orgId (mei seq493): api calls use orgId, route/link building uses orgSlug. Falls back to orgId when absent.

elements.name: + effectiveRole : string
elements.description: The viewer's effective role for the current resource (advisory only, per ADR-015 — role is per-resource, NOT a JWT claim). Used to gate affordance VISIBILITY only; the server guard remains the sole deny-closed boundary.

elements.name: + primary : boolean
elements.description: The clickable identity column (name/title) that owns the row→detail affordance.

elements.name: + width : string
elements.description: CSS width or grow hint, e.g. '32%' / '8rem'.

elements.name: + render : CellRenderer<T>
elements.description: Cell render: a registry hint string or a function. Omit for raw `row[key]`.
